chapter: The Footlight Club and Washington friends
title: Frank Wess goes into Bill Baldwin's band at fifteen
summary: Wess leaves the youth band to become the spark of Baldwin's Colonnade band, for which Malachi credits Billy Roberts's switch to tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Incidentally, Frank Wess, the tenor saxophone player and

flautist, as I said before, he worked with this little band we had when he was 14. By the time he was 15 years old, 15 or 16, he was called to work in one of these bands -- Bill Baldwin's band, that used to work at the Colonnade there. And being as young as he was, he was a phenomenon, too, because he became the spark of the band, you know, being a tenor saxophone player. And I guess, in a way, he can be thankful to Billy Roberts for turning him on to playing the tenor saxophone.
